text: with faster eccentric repetitions (210° per second vs. 20° per second) and Farthing and Chilibeck (64) demonstrated that fast (180° per second) eccentric actions produced greater increases in muscle thickness as compared to both slow (30° per second) and fast concentric actions, but not slow eccentric actions. It should be noted that all of these studies used isokinetic dynamometry, and the results therefore cannot necessarily be generalized to traditional isotonic training methods using coupled concentric and eccentric actions.
